meta.note: Cabin air for each place. Values from NASA documents linked per place. Test pressure in our material table is assumed 1 atm (Space Station / Cygnus cabin).

places.name: Space Station
places.note: Normal cabin air, like at sea level on Earth.

places.name: Spacewalk prep (airlock 'campout')
places.note: Lower pressure, more oxygen, used before spacewalks.

places.name: Moon base
places.note: A planned exploration atmosphere (8.2 psia, 34% oxygen) from NASA studies for habitats with many spacewalks. Actual missions may differ.

places.name: Pressurized rover
places.note: Proposed: NASA rover studies plan the same kind of air as the habitat. Actual vehicles may differ.

places.name: Mars base
places.note: Proposed: NASA exploration-atmosphere studies plan the same kind of air for Mars surface habitats as for Moon bases (8.0 psia and 32% oxygen in 2006, revised to 8.2 psia and 34% in 2012). Actual missions may differ.

warning.text: At 8.2 psia, NASA calculated that oxygen above 31.4% makes materials burn faster: the 34% design point is above that line.
